reproduction_target: Derivation and validation of a 1,209-SNP platform-independent equine parentage panel. Computational target: (1) coordinate standardisation of all downloaded public datasets to EquCab3.0 with UCSC LiftOver; (2) alignment and variant calling of 195 newly generated horse WGS on AWS with the Illumina DRAGEN Bio-IT Platform v4.0 at default parameters against EquCab3.0; (3) gVCF merge and PASS-filtering with bcftools (~5.0M -> ~4.9M variants); (4) integration of the internal callset with 274 public WGS and 364 SNP-array samples under a >=10% sample-presence filter yielding 28,859 positions; (5) array-to-VCF conversion with multiallelic-to-biallelic resolution; (6) linkage-disequilibrium pruning of the 28,859 positions down to the final 1,209 SNPs; (7) evaluation of the 775 autosomal ISAG 2023 parentage SNPs against quality thresholds across WGS platforms (277 failures, 35.7%); (8) PCA / population-structure analysis with the SNPRelate R package; (9) figure generation with ggplot2 and RColorBrewer; (10) a custom filtering script restricting VCFs to the 1,209 positions; (11) a Perl script performing all-pairs parent-offspring opposite-homozygote testing across 195 samples with up to 5 mismatches allowed; (12) a Python script assembling trios from the Perl candidate pairs, checking genetic sex, and applying the ISAG both-parents-homozygous rule with 0-6 mismatches permitted (12 trios recovered, 100% pedigree concordance). Wet-lab target: blood/hair collection, Sbeadex and QIAmp DNA extraction, TruSeq DNA Nano library on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 (CeGaT, 30x/60 GB) and AVITI Cloudbreak Freestyle library on the Element Biosciences AVITI system (Medlabs, Jordan), average depth 29X.
granularity_note: Coarse prose-level decomposition: one step per named tool or per named analysis invocation in MATERIALS AND METHODS plus the analysis sentences carried in RESULTS (the bcftools PASS filter, the >=10% presence filter, the array-to-VCF conversion and the LD pruning are described only in RESULTS, not in Methods). Three unnamed bespoke programs are counted as separate steps because the paper itself names them separately ('a custom filtering script', 'A perl script', 'A Python script'). Wet-lab steps are merged to four (collection, extraction, NovaSeq sequencing, AVITI sequencing) since the paper gives them a single paragraph.

steps.label: Wet-lab: blood (jugular vein) and hair-follicle sample collection from 195 horses 'using standard techniques' / 'according to established protocols'
Wet-lab: DNA isolation with the Sbeadex DNA Purification Kit (Biosearch Technologies) and QIAmp DNA extraction (Qiagen), 'according to the manufacturers' instructions'
Wet-lab: TruSeq DNA Nano (Illumina) library, sequenced on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 at CeGaT GmbH (Germany), 30x / 60 GB output
Wet-lab: AVITI Cloudbreak Freestyle (Element Biosciences) library, sequenced on the Element Biosciences AVITI System at Medlabs (Jordan); average depth across the cohort 29X

Coordinate standardisation of all downloaded datasets to the EquCab3.0 assembly using the UCSC LiftOver tool ('All genomic coordinates from downloaded datasets were standardized to the EquCab3.0 reference assembly using the UCSC LiftOver tool')

Read mapping and variant calling of the 195 internally generated WGS on Amazon Web Services with the Illumina DRAGEN pipeline (Bio-IT Platform version 4.0), aligned to EquCab3.0, 'with default parameters'
Combination of the 195 per-sample VCFs into a single gVCF and retention of variants carrying the PASS filter, using bcftools (~5.0 million -> ~4.9 million variants)

Integration of the quality-filtered internal callset with three external datasets (274 public WGS, 364 SNP-array samples) retaining only positions present in >=10% of samples, yielding 28,859 high-quality positions
Conversion of SNP-array genotypes (GGP Equine 70K, Axiom Equine 670K) to VCF, with duplicate positions representing multiallelic sites resolved to single biallelic calls

Linkage-disequilibrium analysis of the 28,859 positions for independent segregation, reducing the panel to the final 1,209 SNPs ('Linkage disequilibrium patterns were calculated to ensure independent segregation of selected markers')

Evaluation of the 775 autosomal ISAG 2023 parentage SNPs (378 core + 397 backup) against quality thresholds and read depth across all WGS platforms, identifying 277 (35.7%) failures and 498 SNPs overlapping the proposed panel

Cross-validation of the 277 ISAG SNP failures against publicly available VCF files from independent laboratories and pipelines, plus concordance testing across sequencing platforms and alignment pipelines
Principal component analysis / population-structure and breed-clustering assessment using the SNPRelate package in R, run for both the ISAG cross-platform SNP set and the proposed 1,209 SNP set
Figure generation and data visualisation with the ggplot2 and RColorBrewer R packages (breed distribution, chromosome distribution of the 1,209 SNPs, ISAG failure distribution, PCA plots)

Custom filtering script restricting VCF files to the 1,209 high-quality SNP positions ('VCF files were first filtered to retain only the 1,209 high-quality SNP positions using a custom filtering script')

Perl script performing pairwise comparisons between all 195 samples at the 1,209 positions to nominate parent-offspring pairs by the opposite-homozygote rule (parent REF/REF -> offspring not ALT/ALT and vice versa), with up to 5 mismatches permitted per ISAG guidelines

Python script assembling complete trios from the stage-1 candidate pairs, confirming putative sires male and dams female by genetic sex determination, and applying the ISAG both-parents-homozygous rule (offspring cannot be REF/ALT) with 0-6 mismatches permitted; 12 trios recovered from 195 samples and cross-referenced to pedigree records

headline.static_readiness: 0/13 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/13 (0%) RI, 13/13 (100%) NI. Not one computational step clears the RI bar even at the permissive stage-1 prose read, and the reason is a single structural absence: the paper contains no Code availability statement of any kind. There is no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo or Software Heritage identifier anywhere in the manuscript, and the three programs that produce the paper's headline parentage result are described only as 'a custom filtering script', 'A perl script' and 'A Python script'. Nine of the thirteen computational steps therefore score code = 0; the four that reach code = 1 (C1 UCSC LiftOver, C2 DRAGEN, C3 bcftools, and by extension the R work) do so only because the tool is publicly obtainable, not because the invocation is recoverable. The version axis is the second binding constraint: exactly one exact pin exists in the entire paper - 'the Illumina DRAGEN Bio-IT Platform version 4.0' - and even that is a hosted, closed-source, AWS-run commercial pipeline whose behaviour at 'default parameters' cannot be reconstructed from prose. bcftools, UCSC LiftOver, R itself, SNPRelate, ggplot2 and RColorBrewer all appear with no version at all, so twelve of thirteen steps score version = 0. Data is the one axis where the paper is partly strong: 738 of the 833 samples are public and cited concretely (ENA PRJEB14779; a figshare deposit; a University of Kentucky download page), which lifts C1 and C5 to data = 2 and most integration/analysis steps to data = 1. But the 195 newly generated WGS - the samples on which every parentage claim rests - carry no accession and an explicit embargo: 'For reasons of client confidentiality, we may not be able to provide the whole genome but can supply SNPs on reasonable request.' That statement is a request-gated, discretionary release, not controlled access with a governing body, so the five steps entering from those reads score data = 0. The paper's most valuable single artefact for a re-user - the list of the 1,209 selected SNP positions - is presented only as figures and prose counts; no machine-readable position file is deposited. Even a fully cooperative re-user could not begin without first re-deriving the panel from a callset they cannot obtain. Note that this record's ceiling is a stage-1 ceiling: the 13/13 NI result is not a stage-1 artefact here, because the deficits are prose-level absences (no repository, no versions, no accession) that stage-2 code inspection could not repair - there is no code to inspect.
headline.coverage: 13 of 13 computational steps and 4 of 4 wet-lab steps assessed at prose level from the full text (Abstract, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Disclosures, Public Data Sources). Full text retrieved from the bioRxiv HTML full-text view after the JATS XML source endpoint returned HTTP 403. The paper has no Code availability section and no Data availability section in the conventional sense; the closest equivalent is the 'PUBLIC DATA SOURCES' block at the end, which is quoted verbatim in liveness. Four computational steps (C3, C4, C5, C6) are described only in RESULTS and not in MATERIALS AND METHODS, which is itself a granularity hazard: the LD pruning that produces the paper's central deliverable is one sentence long. No supplementary material was fetched; no web search was performed to locate a repository, per protocol - the absence of a stated repository is recorded as a finding, not resolved by searching.

gaps.where: Code availability - all 13 computational steps, and critically C11, C12, C13 (the parentage-calling pipeline)
gaps.missing: The paper contains no code availability statement whatsoever. There is no GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket URL, no Zenodo DOI, no Software Heritage identifier, no supplementary script archive and no statement of intent to deposit code in future. The three programs that generate the paper's headline result are named only by language: 'VCF files were first filtered to retain only the 1,209 high-quality SNP positions using a custom filtering script'; 'A perl script then performed pairwise comparisons between all 195 samples at these positions'; 'A Python script processed the candidate parent-offspring pairs from Stage 1 to assemble complete trios and apply stringent validation criteria'. In addition, the panel-derivation steps (C4 >=10% presence filter, C5 array-to-VCF conversion, C6 LD pruning, C7 ISAG quality-threshold evaluation) name no tool at all and are therefore also code = 0.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the filtering script, the Perl pairwise comparison script and the Python trio assembly/validation script in a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo, together with the driver commands for the >=10% presence filter, the array-to-VCF conversion, the LD pruning and the ISAG quality-threshold evaluation, and the R scripts for the SNPRelate PCA and the ggplot2/RColorBrewer figures. None of this code touches client-confidential genotypes and so carries no embargo risk.

gaps.where: The 195 newly generated whole genome sequences (W3, W4 -> C2, C3, C11, C12, C13) and the derived internal callset
gaps.missing: No accession number in any repository (SRA, ENA, EGA, dbGaP or otherwise) is given for the 195 horse genomes generated in this study. The only statement is, verbatim: 'For reasons of client confidentiality, we may not be able to provide the whole genome but can supply SNPs on reasonable request. Please contact the corresponding author.' This is a discretionary, request-gated, hedged release ('may not be able to'), not controlled access administered by a data access committee, so it does not qualify as controlled-access data with a resolvable identifier. Every parentage validation result in the paper - the 12 trios, the 100% pedigree concordance - depends on data that has no identifier at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the 195 samples in a controlled-access archive (EGA or dbGaP) with a citable accession and a documented access procedure, even if approval is gated. At minimum, deposit the derived per-sample genotypes restricted to the 1,209 panel positions - which the authors already state they can supply - as a versioned public archive with a DOI, rather than as an email request.

gaps.where: The 1,209-SNP panel itself (output of C6) and the 277 failing ISAG SNPs (output of C7)
gaps.missing: The central deliverable of the paper - the list of 1,209 platform-independent SNP positions - is never released as a machine-readable file. It is shown only as a chromosome-distribution histogram (Figure 3) and a Venn-style overlap figure (Figure 2 / Figure 5) with counts in prose. Likewise the 277 ISAG SNPs reported as undetectable by WGS are shown only as Figure 4 and as the count 277 (35.7%) of 775. No supplementary table is cited by identifier for either list, and the intermediate 28,859-position set is not released either. A reader wishing to apply the panel cannot obtain the panel.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit three flat files with EquCab3.0 coordinates, rsIDs and array-probe cross-references: (a) the 1,209 selected positions, (b) the 277 failing ISAG positions, (c) the 28,859-position intermediate set. Place them in a versioned public archive (Zenodo/figshare with a DOI) and cite the DOI in the text.

gaps.where: C1 (UCSC LiftOver), C3 (bcftools), C9 (R and SNPRelate), C10 (ggplot2, RColorBrewer), C11/C12/C13 (Perl and Python interpreters), and the unnamed tooling behind C4-C7
gaps.missing: Exactly one exact version pin appears in the entire paper: 'Our internally generated whole genome sequences were processed using the Illumina DRAGEN Bio-IT Platform version 4.0.' Every other named piece of software is version-free. bcftools is named with no version, UCSC LiftOver with no version, SNPRelate with no version and no R version, ggplot2 and RColorBrewer with no versions, and the Perl and Python scripts with no interpreter version (not even major version: 'A Python script' could be Python 2 or 3). Steps C4, C5, C6 and C7 name no software at all, so there is nothing to pin.
gaps.how_to_close: Report exact versions for every tool and R package, together with the R version and the Perl/Python interpreter versions, ideally as sessionInfo() output and a tool-version table in supplementary material.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment - all 13 computational steps
gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind is claimed. There is no container image or digest, no Dockerfile, no conda/mamba environment YAML, no renv.lock, no requirements.txt or Pipfile.lock for the Python stage, no cpanfile for the Perl stage, and no workflow-manager configuration (Nextflow, Snakemake, WDL, CWL). The compute substrate is named only as 'Amazon Web Services using the Illumina DRAGEN pipeline' with a partner-solutions URL; no AMI, instance type, DRAGEN hardware/FPGA configuration or AWS region is stated, and DRAGEN's results are known to depend on the hardware acceleration configuration.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a container image with a digest (or a conda environment lockfile plus a pinned Python and Perl dependency manifest) covering the whole downstream analysis, and record the DRAGEN deployment configuration - instance type, DRAGEN software build, and any non-default hardware acceleration settings - alongside the pipeline invocation.

gaps.where: C1 (LiftOver chain files), C2 (DRAGEN alignment reference), C4/C5/C6 (harmonised coordinate space), and the ISAG panel definition used in C7
gaps.missing: The reference is given only as the assembly name 'EquCab3.0' with no accession (GCA_002863925.1 vs GCF_002863925.1), no patch or release level, no source URL and no FASTA checksum, and no DRAGEN hash-table build parameters. For the LiftOver step, no chain file is identified - the source assemblies of the downloaded array and WGS datasets (EquCab2.0? assembly-specific array manifests?) are never enumerated, so it is not recoverable which chains were applied to which of the three external data sources. The ISAG 2023 panel of 775 autosomal SNPs is cited as a conference decision ('The ISAG approved 775 autosomal SNPs at their 2023 Equine Committee Conference in Cape Town') with no accessible marker-list artefact, so even the input panel cannot be reconstituted.
gaps.how_to_close: State the reference accession and release, the exact LiftOver chain files and the source assembly for each external dataset, and deposit the 775-SNP ISAG input list as used, with coordinates in the same assembly.

gaps.where: C4 (presence filter), C6 (LD pruning), C7 (ISAG quality thresholds), C13 (genetic sex determination and mismatch tolerance)
gaps.missing: Four decision rules that determine the paper's result are stated without operational parameters. (a) C6, the step that produces the 1,209-SNP panel from 28,859 positions, is described in one sentence - 'Linkage disequilibrium patterns were calculated to ensure independent segregation of selected markers' - with no r-squared threshold, no window size, no step size, no tool and no tie-breaking rule for which member of a linked pair is retained; the reduction from 28,859 to 1,209 is not reproducible from this. (b) C7's 'failed to meet quality thresholds' and 'inadequate quality scores or insufficient read depth' name no numeric cutoffs; the Results mention '10% error rates' and '1X coverage' descriptively but not as thresholds. (c) C4's presence filter is stated as '>=10% of the samples' but does not say whether the denominator is all 833 samples or the per-source cohorts, nor how missing array positions are distinguished from homozygous-reference. (d) C13 confirms 'putative sires were male, and dams were female based on genetic sex determination' with no method, marker set or threshold, and permits '0-6 mismatches' - a range, not a threshold, so the operative cutoff is undetermined.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the LD pruning tool, window, step and r-squared threshold with the marker-retention rule; give the numeric quality and depth cutoffs used to declare an ISAG SNP failed; state the denominator and missingness convention for the >=10% filter; state the sex-determination method and the single mismatch threshold actually applied in the trio validation.

gaps.missing: Two of the three public data sources are moving targets rather than registered, versioned deposits. The 186 University of Kentucky Thoroughbred VCFs are cited as an institutional web page, not a repository accession, with no version, no file list and no checksums; the page content can change or disappear without trace. The 364-sample SNP array dataset is cited as a figshare private-share link (/s/<token>), which is an anonymous sharing URL rather than a public figshare DOI - it is unversioned, revocable by the depositor, and not indexed or archivable. The DRAGEN pipeline itself is cited as an AWS partner marketing page, which is a hosted-service dependency and not a reproducible software artefact. Only the ENA accession PRJEB14779 (88 horses) is a stable, citable identifier.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the figshare deposit by its public DOI and version rather than the /s/ share token; cite the University of Kentucky Thoroughbred diversity data by an archived accession (or mirror it to Zenodo with checksums and record the retrieval date); and replace the AWS partner page with the DRAGEN software build identifier.

gaps.where: C6 (LD pruning marker selection) and C9 (SNPRelate PCA)
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported anywhere in the paper. The LD-pruning marker-selection step in SNPRelate-family tooling (snpgdsLDpruning) traverses markers in a randomised order by default and returns a different retained set on different seeds, which directly changes which 1,209 of the 28,859 positions are selected; the paper reports no seed and no deterministic ordering rule. The PCA in C9 is largely deterministic, but any subsetting or missing-genotype imputation performed by the same package is not described.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the random seed and the RNG state for the LD pruning run, or specify a deterministic marker-ordering rule, and confirm whether the published 1,209-SNP set is seed-stable.
